name: uk.co.fileclerk/filing-tools
title: FileClerk
description: UK company filing deadlines, filed figures and iXBRL validation

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Find a UK company's number from its name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches, each with company_number, company_name, company_status, locality (the town of the registered office), postcode, incorporated_on and match (exact, prefix or partial, with case, punctuation and Ltd, Limited or CIC aside): exact matches first, then active companies, and url (the company's page on FileClerk). For a name with no number: company_number is the input of get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances and run_company_tools. name is 2 to 160 characters; a part of the name is enough. Searches have their own limit of 600 per hour.

name.description: All or a part of the company's name, 2 to 160 characters.

tools.name: get_company_deadlines
tools.description: Is a UK company in good standing on the Companies House register, and what must happen next? Give company_number, or company_name for one call when the name is exact. Returns a verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear), `nearest` (the nearest open date; a payroll row, which is inferred, is left out and `nearest_conditional` holds it with its monthly EPS or PAYE date) and one entry per obligation (annual accounts, confirmation statement, each director's and PSC's identity verification, CT600 return and Corporation Tax payment as estimates, payroll when inferred), each with status, due date, basis (register, estimate or inferred), what can happen if missed and its official source, `rule_url` (the official page for the rule), `evidence_url` (for a Companies House date, the register page that shows the filing), `applies_if` (has_employees on a payroll row) and, for an HMRC payment due on a weekend or bank holiday, `effective_due_on`, the working day before (a Faster Payment or card payment still counts on `due_on`; Companies House dates never move), and `time_limits`, the last day of each open claim or change (amendment, R&D notification, loss and overpayment relief) with what it is for and its source: the soonest of each kind, and both tax periods when an accounts period over 12 months holds two (`accounts_end_on`); `time_limits_more` counts the rest. Only register dates set the verdict: `coming_up` when one is due within `verdict.window_days` (30). `company.pscs` lists each current person with significant control (PSC) with their `shares` and `votes` bands and every nature of control as the register codes it, and `company.last_accounts.figures` gives the last accounts' net assets, turnover and profit as tagged, with `register_url` to open the filed accounts. `company.sic_codes` is the nature of business as SIC codes; get_related_companies gives similar companies and the companies in which it has significant control. `coverage` says what the report reads, `assumptions` (what it assumed for this company: Corporation Tax periods, size, trading, payroll) and `cannot_see` (HMRC records, VAT, taxable profit, AGMs): read it before you flag a date as wrong. A company that a large-company register lists gets a Corporation Tax payment card with no date, because it likely pays in quarterly instalments. 6 to 15 KB for most companies. `detail: "full"` adds each card's details, risks and official links, every open time limit, the timeline, the track record and register changes, and `faq`, common questions about the company answered from its register facts only (no estimate), at about 3 to 4 times the size. Dates are calendar dates in `timezone`; day counts are for `as_of`; `fetched_at` is when the registers were read; a source's `checked_on` is the day FileClerk last checked that rule's page, not the company record. Each obligation's `completion` is done, open or unknown (unknown for every estimate and inferred date: FileClerk cannot see HMRC filings or payments). A community interest company also gets its CIC report (CIC34). `url` is the company's page on FileClerk. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

company_name.description: The company's exact name, in place of company_number, to answer in one call. It answers only when exactly one company has that name (case, punctuation and Ltd, Limited or CIC aside); otherwise it fails with up to 5 candidates and their numbers.

detail.description: How much to return. Left out: summary. full adds each card's details, risks and official links, the timeline, the track record and register changes.

tools.name: get_company_finances
tools.description: Filed figures for a UK company from its last 10 annual accounts on the Companies House register, as tagged in the filed iXBRL: net assets, cash, working capital, average employees, the balance sheet lines, and turnover and profit when the company files them (small and micro companies may leave them out, so they are often null). Also who signed the accounts, when, the accounting standard, audit status, the route they were filed by (filed_via; web_service says WebFiling or Companies House online), and `software`, the software they were made with as named in the filing's hidden tag "Name of production software", when FileClerk knows the name. A year filed as PDF only takes the prior-year column of the next year's iXBRL accounts (source: comparative); else, when FileClerk has read its scanned pages, a figure is kept only when the totals or the OCR digits confirm it (source: pdf-read); scannable is true for a scanned year that FileClerk has not read, reading while a read is queued. `url` is the company's finances page on FileClerk. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description: Find UK companies on the Companies House register by filters, without a name: sic (5-digit SIC code), type (ltd, plc, llp, community-interest-company, private-limited-guarant-nsc, limited-partnership, charitable-incorporated-organisation ...), status (active, dissolved, liquidation ...), location (registered office address), from and to (incorporation dates, YYYY-MM-DD). location takes words of the registered office address, such as a town or a postcode (LS1 or LS1 5EN). Every word must be in the address, so a county finds only the addresses that include it. 50 per page, each with url (the company's page on FileClerk); hits counts every match, pages reach the first 10,000. There is no filter on accounts type (such as dormant or micro-entity) or on whether a company is part of a group: Companies House's search has neither. sic 99999 finds companies that give Dormant Company as their nature of business.

type.description: Company type as Companies House names it, such as ltd, plc, llp or community-interest-company.

status.description: Company status, such as active, dissolved or liquidation.

location.description: Words of the registered office address, such as a town or a postcode (LS1 or LS1 5EN). Every word must be in the address, so a county finds only the addresses that include it.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. A page has 50 companies.

tools.name: search_officers
tools.description: Find UK company officers (directors, secretaries, LLP members) by name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches with officer_id, name and number of appointments. No birth date, nationality or address. get_officer takes an officer_id and gives that officer's companies.

q.description: All or a part of the officer's name, 3 to 160 characters.

tools.name: get_officer
tools.description: Every appointment of one Companies House officer by officer_id (from search_officers): company number and name, role, appointed and resigned dates, company status, current first, with FileClerk's verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear) for companies in its cache. Counts as one lookup.

officer_id.description: The officer_id of one officer, as search_officers returns it.

tools.name: get_related_companies
tools.description: Two lists of other UK companies next to one company, from FileClerk's own copies of the Companies House register. These lists cover only companies on FileClerk: companies someone looked up here, not the whole register. similar: up to 8 active companies like it, a shared SIC code first, then the same postcode district or area, then the same type of last accounts, each with why (reasons). significant_control: up to 25 active companies whose own PSC register names this company, by its company number, as a person with significant control, in company number order, each with when it was notified, the share and vote bands and every nature of control as Companies House codes it; control_total counts them all. Significant control starts above 25% of the shares or votes, so a company in that list is not always a subsidiary in law. read_at is when FileClerk last read its stored copies. It never reads Companies House and counts against no limit. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House. A company_number in get_company_deadlines' company.pscs is this tool's input. url is each company's page on FileClerk.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

tools.name: run_company_tools
tools.description: Every FileClerk tool on one UK company at once: how its last accounts were filed and whether it must move to software by 1 April 2028; whether it can apply to be struck off (pass traded, insolvency and activity as true or false; leave out for verdict answer_questions); its size from the two newest filed accounts (null when they carry too few figures); and the accounts late filing penalty if filed today (null without a due date). `url` is the company's tools explainer page on FileClerk; the same tools run in the Console at /console/tools. Counts as one lookup.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

traded.description: Strike-off answer: true when the company traded or sold stock in the last 3 months.

insolvency.description: Strike-off answer: true when an insolvency process, arrangement or court application is open.

activity.description: Strike-off answer: true when the company did something else in the last 3 months beyond closing down.

tools.name: search_help
tools.description: Search FileClerk's guides to UK company filing: deadlines and penalties, annual accounts, Corporation Tax and the CT600, HMRC error codes, trial balance exports from accounting software, and the ways to file. Any word of `query` can match: a hit that holds more of its words comes first, then one with them in its title. query is up to 200 characters; common words such as "how" and "the" are left out. Up to 12 hits, 5 when limit is left out. Each hit is a whole guide (section null, text its summary) or one of its sections (text the section in full), with checked_on, the day FileClerk last checked the guide against its official sources, and url, its page on FileClerk, the source to cite. It counts against no limit. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

query.description: Words of the question or the topic, such as "HMRC error 3001" or "late filing penalty", up to 200 characters.

limit.description: The most hits to answer, 5 when left out. A number under 1 counts as 1, and one over 12 as 12.
